title: U-Board view document
description: A board as U-Board saves and reads it: a canvas view (widgets placed by position over a background) or a grid view (widgets laid out in order), with the elements it defines. The same rules as validateViewDocument in @iyulab/u-board, except those this schema cannot say: every id — node, connector, decoration, grid item, and those inside a grid's canvas cells — is unique in the document; a widget of type element:<name> names an element the document defines, with props its definition's props schema accepts; a template element's {{values}} are well formed and its markup and CSS keep to the markup policy (no script, no event handlers, URLs only to a fragment, an inline image or a declared resource origin); an element's props schema uses only the keywords it lists; two reference points lie apart on both axes; a value range's min is below its max; a trigger names nodes or items the board places; a component's connectors join its own nodes, its texts use only the parameters it declares, and an instance names a component the board defines, gives only declared parameters in their types and a value to each one its parts use, and its parts' ids (<instance id>/<part id>) are unique in the document like any other. Fields it does not name are allowed, so a document written by a newer version still reads.

components.description: The groups of parts this board draws more than once, by name. An instance places one.

component.description: A group of parts defined once and drawn by each instance that places it: nodes, connectors between them and decorations, placed from the component's origin. In any text of its parts, {{name}} stands for the parameter name's value; a text that is only {{name}} takes the value itself. Each part is drawn with the id <instance id>/<part id>.

params.description: The parameters it takes: a JSON Schema object schema using the keywords an element's props schema uses. A parameter's default stands for an instance that gives none.

componentNode.description: A node of a component: a canvas node without anchored, which its instance gives. Its id has no / and no {{…}}.

instance.description: A component drawn on the board, its origin at (x, y), with a value for each of its parameters.

anchored.description: As a node's: whether (x, y) is a coordinate in the background's real space. Its nodes take it.

params.description: A value for each parameter of the component, by name.

items.description: In the order they are shown: left to right, then top to bottom.

columns.description: Columns at full width. Only 12 for now; absent means 12.

symbols.description: Drawings the board's template elements share, by name: <use href="#name"/> places one. Markup is held to the template policy and has no values.

viewBox.description: min-x min-y width height, such as "0 0 24 24".

accent.description: The board's accent: the colour its widgets and elements fill and highlight with, in place of the theme's primary colour. Absent means the theme's.

appearance.description: The tone the board is drawn in. Absent means light.

elements.description: The elements this board defines, by name. A widget of type element:<name> places one.

elementDefinition.description: Drawn once for each widget that places it. A template element is markup with {{prop}} values, isolated from the rest of the page and running no script; a script element runs its script in a sandboxed frame with no network, its data arriving as props.

props.description: The props it takes: a JSON Schema object schema using only type, enum, const, properties, required, items, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, title, description and default.

template.description: HTML or SVG markup with {{name}}, {{#list}}…{{/list}} and {{^flag}}…{{/flag}}; every value is escaped.

script.description: The code a script element runs. It receives its props through ub.onProps.

style.description: CSS for its own markup only.

size.description: Its own size: the box a canvas node placing it takes when it gives none, and the height a grid item placing it takes when it gives none.

resources.description: The https origins it loads anything from — host and port, nothing after.

referencePoints.description: Two points of the image and the coordinates they stand for, apart on both axes in the image and in their coordinates.

node.description: A widget placed on a canvas view.

width.description: The box's width. Left out: the width of the element it places (its size), else 160.

height.description: The box's height. Left out: the height of the element it places (its size), else 100.

anchored.description: Whether (x, y) is a coordinate meaningful in the background's real space, or a free position.

caption.description: A name drawn under the node's box, outside it — a device's name under its icon.

gridItem.description: What a grid view holds in a cell: a widget, or a canvas of its own — not both.

gridWidgetItem.description: A widget in a grid view and the room it takes.

span.description: Columns it spans at full width. Absent means 4.

spanMedium.description: Columns it spans at medium width, where the grid has 6. Absent means half of span, rounded up.

rowSpan.description: Rows it spans at medium and full width — a map or large panel beside a column of smaller cards, which the items after it fill in order. Absent means 1; a narrow grid ignores it.

height.description: Its height in pixels. Absent means the widget's own height.

gridCanvasItem.description: A canvas in a grid view's cell and the room it takes — the spatial panel of a mixed board, the cards around it laid out by the grid.

span.description: Columns it spans at full width. Absent means 4.

spanMedium.description: Columns it spans at medium width, where the grid has 6. Absent means half of span, rounded up.

rowSpan.description: Rows it spans at medium and full width — a map or large panel beside a column of smaller cards, which the items after it fill in order. Absent means 1; a narrow grid ignores it.

height.description: Its height in pixels. Absent means the height that keeps the canvas's proportions.

cellCanvas.description: The spatial layer of a canvas view, drawn fitted to its cell. The board's elements, symbols and triggers stay on the board; a connector joins two nodes of the same cell.

connector.description: A line between two nodes, from the edge of one node's box to the edge of the other's. Connectors joining the same two nodes are drawn side by side.

label.description: Text on the line, on a chip of the board's paper. With a label binding, {{value}} (or {{value | fixed:N}}) in it is where the bound value goes: "{{value | fixed:1}} Mbps".

labelAt.description: Where along the line the label sits, from 0 (the fromNodeId end) to 1 (the toNodeId end); the middle when left out.

labelSize.description: The label's font size in scene units; its chip grows with it. 11 when left out — a board drawn large (a kiosk, a wall) sets it so the label reads at the size the board is seen.

style.description: How the line is drawn; each part left out takes the board's connector look.

stroke.description: A colour in the forms a decoration takes.

arrow.description: Which ends carry an arrowhead: end points at the toNodeId node, start at the fromNodeId node.

route.description: The way the line runs: straight (when left out) from box to box, orthogonal — out of the side facing the other node, one turn at the middle of the gap, into the other's facing side — or curved, bowing to the left of the way it runs (from fromNodeId toward toNodeId), as flows on a map are drawn.

bindings.description: Live values for the label and the style, by path — the same shape as a widget's bindings.

placement.description: A point of a box: start is the left, end the right.

shape.description: A purely visual decoration: a labeled frame or a text, with no widget and no binding.

radius.description: Rounds the corners; at most half the shorter side is drawn.

label.description: The frame's name, drawn inside it at labelAt, in the stroke's colour.

labelAt.description: Where inside the frame its name sits; top-start when left out.

labelSize.description: The name's font size; 13 when left out.

labelFill.description: The name's colour; the stroke's when left out.

anchor.description: Which point of the text's box x/y is; top-start when left out.

background.description: Fills a box around the text, so it reads over what lies under it.

widget.description: What a node or grid item shows. A prepared widget's type and props belong to the widget library; a type of element:<name> places an element this document defines. bindings name the props replaced by a live value.

binding.description: A reference to a value in an external system, read through an adapter. ref's shape is up to the adapter.

valueMap.description: Source values to the values a prop takes: values by text, then ranges, then otherwise.

valueRange.description: From min up to but not including max; at least one bound, and min below max when both are given.

stateRule.description: The states a part can be in, named from the reading of one of its widget's bindings (from: its key) — the source's value before that binding's map, looked up in map (values by text, then ranges, then otherwise). A reading the map names nothing for is no state. looks: how each state is shown, by name.

trigger.description: What the board does when something happens on it: on an event, only when a part is in one of the given states (if given), do the actions in order. A viewer runs triggers; nothing a trigger does writes to the systems the board reads.

oneOf.description: Opens a link in a new tab: an https:// address or a path on this installation; {{node}}, {{state}} and {{board}} are filled in.

stateLook.description: How a part is shown while in a state: a ring of colour around it (outline), blinking (blink — not where the reader asks for reduced motion), or not drawn (hidden).

outline.description: A ring around the part: a colour, or a theme colour's name (positive, warning, negative, accent) drawn in the board's tone.
